candidate.title: fC-CET
candidate.scope: The fC-CET row of the supplied Illumina poster: bisulfite-free selective labeling and enrichment of genomic 5fC, followed by adapter ligation/PCR that encodes target sites as C-to-T changes and a final purified DNA library. The card title, row label and independently matching collection-page heading establish this target. Adjacent TAmC-Seq, fC-Seal and CAB-Seq rows (including the CAB-Seq control branch) are separate contextual assays, not alternatives or branches of fC-CET. The row has a single linear route. Primary-paper evidence clarifies the target adduct, strand-selective pull-down and library/readout interface; unshown experimental controls, library internals and other applications are outside this schematic scope.

states.label: Genomic DNA containing 5fC among cytosine forms
features: Biological target is 5-formylcytosine (5fC) in genomic DNA; the DNA itself is the chemical substrate.
Input cartoon displays ordinary C, 5mC, 5hmC, 5fC and 5caC on a DNA backbone; these are illustrative base classes, not a required sequence or stoichiometry.
The separate yellow 5fc residue icon identifies the target; it is not a separate material input or processing step.

states.label: Released, enriched target-bearing DNA strands after pull-down, NaOH and DTT
features: Preparation history: AI-labeled and biotinylated DNA has undergone streptavidin capture, removal of strands without 5fC by NaOH, and DTT-mediated release.

The modified 5fC-derived base remains in the DNA template for subsequent PCR readout.

states.label: Purified fC-CET DNA library
features: Final product is the DNA line at the end of the fC-CET row, with the C-to-T sequence encoding established during PCR.

Downstream sequencing can identify candidate 5fC positions from target-associated C-to-T changes and locate enriched regions; sequencing is described in the sources but is not a separate operation drawn in this row.
Affinity enrichment provides relative representation of selected DNA, not a direct absolute fraction of 5fC at each genomic site; an individual T observation is not by itself proof of 5fC.

operations.label: Azido 1,3-indandione (AI)
operations.description: AI reacts selectively with 5fC residues in genomic DNA to produce the 5fC-AI adduct bearing an azido handle. The target-containing DNA backbone is retained; the output differs by target-specific chemical derivatization.
operations.mechanism: Source-supported cyclization labeling of 5fC with an azido derivative of 1,3-indandione. The label both supplies a conjugation handle and enables the later PCR readout.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a chemical tag at the original 5fC position on the same DNA sequence; no sequence conversion is depicted at this boundary.

operations.label: Pulldown, NaOH and DTT
operations.description: The composite depicted block captures biotin-tagged DNA on streptavidin beads, uses NaOH to remove strands without 5fC while retaining biotinylated strands, then uses DTT to cleave the biotin linkage and release target-bearing strands. Output is enriched, released DNA with the residual target-linked handle shown as N3-SH.
operations.mechanism: Biotin–streptavidin affinity capture followed by strand separation/removal under NaOH and reductive cleavage of the disulfide-bearing tag by DTT. Transient bead attachment is internal to this broad depicted block.
operations.information_effect: Selects target-bearing strands rather than merely preserving both strands of a captured duplex. Removing 5fC-null strands increases the target-associated C-to-T signal available for sequencing; selection does not establish perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation and PCR
operations.description: Released, enriched DNA is converted to an adapter-bearing amplified DNA library. PCR reads the chemically derivatized 5fC position as T, producing the depicted C-to-T sequence change. This is a copying/readout event, not a depicted direct chemical conversion of the genomic 5fC residue into thymine.
operations.mechanism: Adapter ligation and PCR remain one broad operation as drawn. The primary implementation uses TELP for this library interface; TELP is a component of fC-CET here, not a separate target workflow. The primary source reports cyclization-enabled C-to-T readout while leaving its detailed molecular mechanism unresolved.
operations.information_effect: Converts target-position chemical information into a sequence difference carried by amplified DNA. The genomic sequence provides positional identity; T at a former target C supports base-resolution 5fC detection after sequencing, subject to background conversion and selection bias.
